title: The Stick Fort Windbreak
logline: Pip's blueprint for the stick fort is perfect. Nimbus holds sticks with careful little gusts — mostly helpfully. The fort only works when Nimbus's 'wrong' crooked wall turns out to be the windbreak that makes it cozy.
starting_goal: Build a stick fort big enough for two
friction_source: A perfect plan meets a builder who helps by feel
character_want: Pip: competent-wanted — the blueprint is his bid; bending it feels like erasing himself
power_usage: Gust-held sticks speed the build and misplace one wall; hands could do both, slower and less funny
escalation: Escalation by kind: blueprint -> corrected crooked wall -> Pip secretly straightening it nightly while Nimbus secretly re-crooks it, each baffled
emotional_beat: They nap in the fort; the straight walls look right, the crooked wall is the side that blocks the wind — Pip leaves it, and sketches a new blueprint with one crooked line on purpose
rewatch_detail: The crooked wall's shadow covers Pip's reading spot in the final scene — the plan served him by accident
distinctness_note: The plan is not wrong and reality is not cruel; the fix is a hybrid of both methods, not abandonment of the plan

title: The Dam That Worked Too Well
logline: A stick-and-stone dam to send water to the garden bed works perfectly — so perfectly the boat lane goes dry. Fixing one thirst created another.
starting_goal: Divert a little stream water to the garden bed
friction_source: A working solution with an invisible cost downstream
character_want: Both: competent-wanted — the dam is their first joint engineering success, and admitting its flaw hurts
power_usage: None; stream engineering only
escalation: Escalation by kind: dam -> deeper dam -> the paper boats grounding mid-regatta-practice while the garden floods slightly
emotional_beat: They rebuild the dam with a gate: open for boats, closed for watering; the failure becomes the mechanism
rewatch_detail: The stream's sound changes pitch as the water drops — an audio callback audible from the first dam scene
distinctness_note: Cause and consequence are both the characters' own success; no accident, no weather, no villain

title: A Roof for the Snail
logline: A real raincloud is coming — the world's, not Nimbus. The pair races to roof the snail's corner. Nimbus watches another cloud rain 'his' garden and feels something he can't name.
starting_goal: Build shelter for the snail before the natural rain arrives
friction_source: A deadline from nature, plus Nimbus's strange jealousy of a cloud that isn't him
character_want: Nimbus: needed — the world's rain does his job for free; he must learn his value was never the water
power_usage: None; the rain is the world's, which is precisely the point
escalation: Escalation by kind: leaf roof -> bark roof -> a double roof 'in case', while the cloud on the horizon moves at weather speed, not story speed
emotional_beat: The rain comes gently; the roof holds; Nimbus watches the garden drink someone else's rain and finds he is glad — mostly. One small private drip escapes anyway, and Pip pretends not to see
rewatch_detail: The horizon cloud is visible, tiny, from the first scene — the deadline is shown, never stated
distinctness_note: Nimbus meets the fact that weather exists without him; identity drama with zero power use

title: The Windsock That Reads Nimbus
logline: Nimbus can't feel his own leaks coming. Pip builds a windsock on the hill — not for the world's wind, for Nimbus's. Now Nimbus can watch himself feel.
starting_goal: Build a way for Nimbus to notice his own gusts before they happen
friction_source: You cannot read your own face; the leaky friend wants a mirror
character_want: Nimbus: wanted-but-safe — self-knowledge as protection from his own body
power_usage: The entire device exists to measure Nimbus's emotional micro-gusts; the premise is the expressive philosophy instrumented
escalation: Escalation by kind: windsock -> calibrated ribbons for feelings (pale=worry, brisk=excitement) -> Nimbus performing feelings at the sock to test it, which produces no wind at all
emotional_beat: The sock flops still during his forced tests and stirs only at a real laugh; sincerity, measured. He stops performing and starts noticing
rewatch_detail: Each ribbon color maps to a feeling shown in an earlier episode; the mapping is never explained, only shown
distinctness_note: The characters build a tool to read the show's own central mechanic — self-aware without breaking the fourth wall

title: The Bridge the Snail Tested
logline: The stepping stones wobble. Pip designs a plank bridge with counterweights; Nimbus ferries pebble ballast by gust. The first official crossing belongs to the snail, who takes forty minutes and finds a gap.
starting_goal: Replace the wobbly stepping stones with a small bridge
friction_source: A designed system meets a user with different physics
character_want: Pip: competent-wanted — the bridge passing its 'inspection' matters more to him than the crossing
power_usage: Gust-ferried pebble ballast is faster than carrying; the bridge itself is pure carpentry
escalation: Escalation by kind: plank -> counterweights -> official opening ceremony with a ribbon the snail ignores by sliding under
emotional_beat: The snail finds the one gap Pip missed; instead of despair, Pip carves a tiny snail gate into the design — the user's needs amend the blueprint
rewatch_detail: The snail begins its crossing in scene two and completes it in the final shot — a slow-motion race against the whole episode
distinctness_note: Engineering succeeds via user feedback, not via the plan; the care-receiver is the QA department

title: The Banner Says Weather Included
logline: Community day needs a welcome banner. Nimbus is terrified his worry-drip will spot the paint. Worrying about dripping causes dripping. The banner gets its decoration from the thing they feared.
starting_goal: Paint and hang the welcome banner spot-free
friction_source: Anxiety about a leak manufactures the leak (self-fulfilling worry loop)
character_want: Nimbus: needed — being trusted with community day is everything; spotting the banner would un-earn it
power_usage: Worry-drip lands on wet paint; the loop of worry->drip->worry is the engine and requires the leak
escalation: Escalation by kind: hovering far from the banner (drips from range) -> holding his breath -> Pip's drip-shield contraption of leaves that concentrates every drip into one dramatic drop
emotional_beat: The one big drop lands in the blue paint and blooms into a flower shape; they paint more drops on purpose; the banner reads as a garden — weather included
rewatch_detail: The accidental drop-bloom appears in the background as a motif on later community decorations
distinctness_note: Self-fulfilling anxiety as mechanism; the feared event becomes the artwork — reframe at the visual level

title: The Lightened Pack
logline: Pip packs for the hilltop hike: rope, umbrellas, spare maps. Nimbus quietly removes 'silly weight' to help. Halfway up, the world sends a light rain — and the umbrellas are home.
starting_goal: Hike to the hilltop with a sensible pack
friction_source: Secret help that removes exactly what will be needed
character_want: Nimbus: needed — lightening Pip's load felt like love; confessing means owning the coming wet
power_usage: Nimbus cannot stop the world's rain (not his, not allowed to); any drizzle works, his guilt is the point
escalation: Escalation by kind: missing scarf (fine) -> missing rope (hm) -> missing umbrellas (oh no), each discovered one hill-steeper than the last
emotional_beat: They share one big leaf as a hood; Pip lists the walk as 'very good' on his map; Nimbus re-packs openly next time, and Pip lets him remove one thing
rewatch_detail: Each removed item is visible in the home scene behind Nimbus as he 'tidies' — the audience knows before Pip does
distinctness_note: Help-without-asking as the error; the world's weather supplies consequences Nimbus did not cause

title: Winter Corner
logline: The garden bed must be tucked in for the cold season. Pip winterizes everything — including the kite, the boat, and, nearly, the snail. Preparing for a goodbye is still a goodbye.
starting_goal: Prepare the garden and its small life for the cold season
friction_source: Care expressed as control meets a season that doesn't negotiate
character_want: Pip: wanted — if everything is prepared, nothing is lost; Nimbus: needed — the garden slept fine before he existed
power_usage: None
escalation: Escalation by kind: mulch -> windscreens -> a tiny blanket stitched for the snail's shell, which the snail wears exactly once, out of politeness
emotional_beat: The last warm day they spend sitting in the garden doing nothing preparable; the blanket stays on the shelf as a winter flag
rewatch_detail: The snail's blanket migrates: shell -> shelf -> kite tail in a later episode
distinctness_note: Seasonal change as the problem; care must learn the difference between protecting and holding on

title: Two Breakfasts
logline: Each secretly decides to surprise the other with breakfast. Neither can ask what the other is doing. Both cook a full breakfast. Eating both breakfasts to protect both feelings becomes the challenge.
starting_goal: Each wants to surprise the other with breakfast
friction_source: Two secret kind plans colliding in one kitchen space
character_want: Both: needed — each breakfast is a belonging bid that must not be seen to fail
causal_detail: Mutual secret plans (E4 bid collision): two independent kind intentions produce double the result
power_usage: None
escalation: Escalation by kind: decoy errands to clear the kitchen -> both hiding ingredients in the same cupboard and each thinking the doubling stock is their own -> the ceremonial serving of two full trays
emotional_beat: Halfway through two breakfasts they trade trays; the muffin-stall inherits the leftovers with a joint note signed by both
rewatch_detail: Ingredient quantities in the cupboard visibly double between scenes for attentive viewers
distinctness_note: No error, no weather, no third party — the collision of two kindnesses is the entire plot

title: The Great Leaf Sort
logline: A windy night scatters leaves everywhere. Pip invents a taxonomy: by size, color, and curl. Nimbus's pile method is 'all of them, over there'. The leaves migrate nightly, as leaves do.
starting_goal: Clear the paths and beds after the windy night
friction_source: A classification system versus a volume approach, against entropy
character_want: Pip: competent-wanted — order restored is his love language; Nimbus: needed — done fast is help you can feel
power_usage: Nimbus's tidying gusts redistribute leaves into new disorder; the story works with any two cleanup styles
escalation: Escalation by kind: sorted piles -> labeled piles -> a cairn of 'uncategorizable' leaves that achieves monument status overnight
emotional_beat: The uncategorizable cairn becomes the garden's leaf-mold corner — the failure pile turns out to be the garden's pantry
rewatch_detail: One red leaf keeps escaping every pile; it is finally filed in a class of one
distinctness_note: Entropy as the antagonist; the resolution dignifies the messy pile instead of defeating it

title: The Petal Blockade
logline: Fallen petals clog the boat lane of the stream. Scooping them out feels like throwing away a parade. The pair races the petals downstream before the whole lane jams.
starting_goal: Clear the petal clog from the stream's boat lane
friction_source: The mess is beautiful; removing it is necessary and a little sad
character_want: Both: competent-wanted — keeping the lane clear is their duty to the boat game
power_usage: None; scooping and raking only
escalation: Escalation by kind: scooping -> a competition for fastest scoop -> splashing that soaks both and jams the lane faster
emotional_beat: The last scooped armful is pressed between planks into petal paper; the jam becomes the artifact
rewatch_detail: The pressed petal paper becomes the banner backing in a later community scene
distinctness_note: Cleanup of something lovely; reluctance as the honest emotion inside a chore

title: The Winnowing
logline: Pip knocks over the seed jars; three seed kinds mix on the ground. Sorting by eye fails. Nimbus's gentle gust lifts the light husks and leaves the heavy seeds — the wind does the sorting.
starting_goal: Un-mix three kinds of spilled seeds before planting day
friction_source: A physical mixture too fine for fingers
character_want: Pip: competent-wanted — the spill was his clumsiness; fixing it invisibly would erase it
power_usage: Calibrated mild gust separates husk from seed (real winnowing physics); the ONLY premise where the power is the correct tool — used once, and it still needs Pip's observation to aim it
escalation: Escalation by kind: tweezer sorting -> sorting contest -> a sneeze-level gust that redistributes everything and forces the honest solution
emotional_beat: Pip admits the spill to the board unprompted; the note back says mixed seed rows grow the best salads — and next year's jars get lids
rewatch_detail: The seed kinds are color-coded for viewers; the winnowing visibly separates them by weight for real
distinctness_note: The single true 'power as correct tool' case, grounded in real physics (winnowing), kept rare on purpose

title: The Plans That Rained Themselves
logline: Nimbus rains a little in his sleep when he dreams. One night he naps beside Pip's plan-board. The ink runs. Tomorrow's perfect plans are now watercolor.
starting_goal: Recover a day whose plans were washed out
friction_source: An involuntary, unconscious leak destroys the friend's records
character_want: Pip: competent-wanted — his plans are his memory; Nimbus: needed — his own body betrayed the friendship in his sleep
causal_detail: Sleep-drizzle: an unconscious, mild rain tied to dreaming — an extension of the expressive philosophy, flagged as a hypothesis for owner review
power_usage: Sleep-drizzle blurs the plans; the day itself is run from memory, weather-free
escalation: Escalation by kind: Pip reconstructs the plan from memory (wrong order) -> improvises -> discovers the improvised order is better and quietly re-inks the board to match reality
emotional_beat: Nimbus offers to sleep outside; Pip moves the board instead — the friendship adjusts the furniture, not the friend
rewatch_detail: The blurred plans form a readable watercolor of the hill — the board is later framed as art
distinctness_note: Loss of artifacts as stakes; the fix is protecting the friend from guilt, not restoring the paper

title: The Kite Patch
logline: The kite is torn. Patching is easy; waiting for the paste to set is impossible. Nimbus's little drying gusts wrinkle the patch twice. Patience, not paste, is the repair.
starting_goal: Repair the kite's tear before the afternoon breeze
friction_source: Drying faster is available and harmful; help must be withheld
character_want: Nimbus: needed — doing nothing while a friend waits feels like refusing to help
power_usage: Premature drying gusts wrinkle the patch; the mechanism is specifically wind-drying, but the lesson is his restraint, not the wind
escalation: Escalation by kind: one test gust (wrinkle) -> re-paste, hold back, fail again (wrinkle) -> Pip builds a drip-free, gust-free waiting tent and they wait inside it together
emotional_beat: The third patch dries untouched because Nimbus tells it a story instead of drying it; the kite flies with one visible seam, flown proudly
rewatch_detail: The patch seam flutters visibly in the final flight — the scar stays on screen as a feature
distinctness_note: A deliberate development of Show Bible example 3 (premature drying) with the restraint moved into the character, not the technique

title: Two Stones for One
logline: A stepping stone cracks through. It cannot be glued. Two smaller stones might do one stone's job — if they can be tested by a hop, a wobble, and a very brave snail.
starting_goal: Restore the stream crossing after a stone cracks
friction_source: Irreversible damage; the repair must be a different thing, not the same thing restored
character_want: Both: competent-wanted — the crossing is their daily route; its loss is personal
power_usage: None; Nimbus tests stones by floating down onto them, which is locomotion, not a power
escalation: Escalation by kind: single replacement (too small) -> two stones (wobbly) -> a tested, settled pair with a snail-sized bypass ramp
emotional_beat: The cracked stone is not discarded — it becomes the path's 'remember to step gently' marker at the path's start
rewatch_detail: The crack in the old stone matches the shape of the stream bend — a visual rhyme findable on rewatch
distinctness_note: Repair-as-redesign; the broken object is memorialized rather than fixed or discarded

title: The Formal Apology
logline: After their first real argument (whose fault the crashed cart was — both, partly), each apologizes in their own grammar: Pip writes a structured apology with headings; Nimbus rains a small formal pattern. Both are ridiculous. Both are sincere.
starting_goal: Each wants to apologize properly
friction_source: Two apology languages that cannot be read by the other
character_want: Both: wanted — the argument threatened the bond; the apology must be seen to be real
power_usage: Nimbus's drizzle-pattern apology (dots and dashes of rain) is only readable as feeling, not words; any sincere gesture works, his is legible weather
escalation: Escalation by kind: apology draft one (too cold) -> draft two (too long, laminated) -> Nimbus's rain-morse that Pip carefully transcribes wrong, apologizing back for the misreading
emotional_beat: They laugh at the laminated apology together, in the rain of the second apology, and the argument ends somewhere inside the laughter
rewatch_detail: The rain-morse pattern actually spells a rhythm reused as the pair's reconciliation motif in later episodes
distinctness_note: Relationship repair as literal translation problem between two expressive systems

title: The Gap the Snail Kept Finding
logline: The fence has a gap; the snail keeps finding it and heading for the road. Pip builds a five-layer barrier. The snail, unhurried, demonstrates each layer's flaw across one long afternoon.
starting_goal: Keep the snail safely away from the road
friction_source: Engineering against a slow, patient, unstoppable user
character_want: Pip: competent-wanted — outplanned by a snail is a specific humiliation; Nimbus: needed — guarding is helping too
power_usage: A shade-gust redirects the snail once; the story is about the barrier arms race, not weather
escalation: Escalation by kind: plank -> plank with moat -> moat with drawbridge -> surveillance schedule, each defeated slowly and visibly
emotional_beat: They plant the snail's favorite greens on the safe side; the gap stays, guarded by salad; the snail chooses to stay
rewatch_detail: The snail tests layers in the order Pip built them, visibly learning — a whole silent subplot
distinctness_note: Repair solved by attraction rather than exclusion; the antagonist is a snail's honesty about what it wants

title: The Pumpkin Roll
logline: The garden's one giant pumpkin must reach the stall. Nimbus's excitement-gust starts it rolling early. Stopping it fails; steering it like a boat down the lane becomes the day's sport.
starting_goal: Deliver the pumpkin to the stall intact
friction_source: A rolling pumpkin obeys slopes, not wishes
character_want: Nimbus: needed — his leak caused it; fixing it is his amends; Pip: competent-wanted — the route plan never survived first contact
power_usage: The starting gust is Nimbus's excitement; steering is done with boards and banking, not powers
escalation: Escalation by kind: braking (fails) -> barrier (vaults it) -> coordinated banking turns shouted like sailors, until the pumpkin parks itself at the stall to applause
emotional_beat: The stall pins a ribbon on the pumpkin: 'arrived by itself, apparently'; Nimbus's relieved laugh-gust rolls it the final inch onto the scale
rewatch_detail: The audience sees Nimbus swell with excitement a full shot before the first roll — the signature forecast beat
distinctness_note: The chase is reframed as steering; the characters succeed by joining the physics, not fighting it

title: Twelve Eggs, One Bridge
logline: The stall's eggs must cross the wobbly pre-bridge stones. Pip's cushioning ritual is thorough; the journey is long; Nimbus's job is shade and morale. The near-slip belongs to both of them.
starting_goal: Carry a dozen eggs across the stream before the stall opens
friction_source: Fragile cargo, a wobbly crossing, and a clock
character_want: Both: trusted — the stall trusted them with the fragile thing; trust is the cargo too
power_usage: Nimbus shades the eggs with his body (position, not power); no weather is deployed
escalation: Escalation by kind: cushion nest -> cushion nest in a sling -> sling carried at funeral pace while the stall's queue shadow grows across the path
emotional_beat: One egg cracks on the final step; they deliver eleven and the truth; the stall bakes the twelfth on the spot and shares it back
rewatch_detail: The queue's shadow inches across the path in every scene — the clock is visual
distinctness_note: Partial failure delivered honestly; the community absorbs the loss and closes the loop kindly

title: The Leaky Bucket Brigade
logline: The hilltop seedling is thirsty; the only bucket leaks. Filling faster does not beat leaking always. The answer is not a better bucket but a different water.
starting_goal: Get stream water to the hilltop seedling
friction_source: The transport vessel defeats the transport goal
character_want: Both: needed — the seedling is their shared promise to the garden
power_usage: Nimbus's one small rain could water it directly — and is the wrong answer they deliberately refuse (dependence avoided); the bucket must be beaten honestly
escalation: Escalation by kind: faster trips -> two buckets, both leaky, staggered -> a relay of leaf-cups that loses half the water to laughter
emotional_beat: They dig a shallow trickle-channel from the stream and watch water walk uphill-adjacent by itself; the seedling drinks from the world's own plumbing
rewatch_detail: Water loss is marked by a dark line down each carrier's front that resets scene by scene — the measure of stubbornness
distinctness_note: Explicit refusal of the power-solution in favor of an observed real-world one — anti-F1 by design

title: The Snail Express
logline: The snail must be home across the path before dark. A leaf-sled, a drizzle trail for glide, and a passenger with no concept of urgency make the slowest express in the world.
starting_goal: Carry the snail home before dark
friction_source: A passenger whose nature is slowness, against a sunset
character_want: Both: needed — the snail cannot hurry; the helpers must learn its speed is not a malfunction
power_usage: A drizzle trail lubricates the leaf-sled (snails glide on moisture — real biology); the sled is the transport, the drizzle is the rails
escalation: Escalation by kind: sled -> sled plus drizzle rails -> a gentle downhill detour that arrives fast but at the wrong door, requiring one uphill apology lap
emotional_beat: The snail arrives at full dark, unbothered, and begins its evening meal as if nothing happened; the helpers lie on the path, heroic and damp
rewatch_detail: The sun's shadow-line races the sled across scenes — a visible finish line approaching
distinctness_note: Speed versus a slow being resolved by respecting its physics; the power serves the passenger's biology

title: Smooth Ones, Interesting Ones
logline: The garden border needs pebbles. Pip collects smooth ones by rule; Nimbus collects interesting ones by joy. Two collections, one border, zero agreement.
starting_goal: Collect enough pebbles to edge the garden bed
friction_source: Two incompatible collection philosophies share one purpose
character_want: Both: wanted — each collection is a self-portrait; editing it feels like being edited
power_usage: None; Nimbus spots pebbles from hover-height, which is locomotion, not power
escalation: Escalation by kind: two piles -> a disputed middle pile -> classification arguments over one legendary pebble that is both smooth AND interesting
emotional_beat: The border is laid alternating smooth and interesting, with the legendary pebble at the gate; the pattern is later called 'the friendship edge'
rewatch_detail: The legendary pebble appears in the background of earlier scenes before its starring episode
distinctness_note: Collection-as-identity; the compromise is a visible pattern with a name, seeding a recurring motif

title: Apples Before the Snail
logline: Windfall apples must be gathered before the snail reaches them. Speed bruises; care is slow. The race against one slow snail teaches two fast friends about gentle hands.
starting_goal: Collect the windfall apples before the snail eats them
friction_source: A deadline measured in snail-speed that still manages to be urgent
character_want: Both: competent-wanted — harvest is the garden's exam; bruised apples are visible mistakes
power_usage: Nimbus's shade keeps picked apples cool (body position); rushing is the mechanism, not weather
escalation: Escalation by kind: basket race -> bruised apples -> the snail, ahead of them both, samples exactly one apple, politely, and stops
emotional_beat: The bruised apples become today's muffins for the stall; the snail's one sampled apple gets a plaque: 'taste-tester'
rewatch_detail: The snail's approach is measurable scene by scene against the apple row — the slowest countdown in the series
distinctness_note: The deadline antagonist is gentle and entitled to its share; winning includes feeding the rival

title: Dew Collectors
logline: Dawn dew is the garden's gentlest water. Collecting it means waking early, moving softly, and discovering that the biggest dewdrop of all is snoring above the leaf pile.
starting_goal: Collect dew for the seedling tray before the sun takes it
friction_source: A fragile, time-limited resource and one collector who IS moisture
character_want: Both: needed — dawn work is the garden's quiet duty; Nimbus wants to prove he can be gentle on purpose
power_usage: Nimbus's sleepy drip is mistaken for a giant dewdrop; the mix-up is the gag, any drip would do — but his is the honest one
escalation: Escalation by kind: leaf-cup tipping -> a dew-spoon -> following the 'biggest dewdrop' and nearly harvesting a sleeping friend
emotional_beat: The tray is filled with one spoon to spare; the spare drop is given back to the stream 'for the fish', a ritual born on screen
rewatch_detail: The light changes measurably from blue to gold across the episode — the deadline is the color grade
distinctness_note: The collector is made of the collected; identity gag grounded in a real morning chore

title: The Found-Things Board
logline: After the windy night: a feather, a button, a bottle cap, a ribbon-less kite tail. Pip catalogs; Nimbus displays. The shelf of found things becomes the village's found board by accident.
starting_goal: Sort the objects the wind delivered
friction_source: Catalog versus display; ownership of wind-brought things is unclear
character_want: Both: competent-wanted — each believes his system serves the finder best
power_usage: None; the delivering wind was the world's
escalation: Escalation by kind: shelf -> categories -> a hand-drawn label system so good that notes begin arriving: 'lost: one button' — the collection becomes a service
emotional_beat: The button goes home to its owner by note; the feather stays; the board gets an official corner in the village layer
rewatch_detail: Every found object was visible mid-flight in the opening storm-gust montage — the origin story is shown, not told
distinctness_note: A collecting premise that mutates into community infrastructure; the third-force layer builds itself

title: The Stream's Wrong Voice
logline: The stream sounds wrong — a branch is damming it upstream. Pip cannot start the day without the right burble. Nimbus tries to drizzle the sound back. The fix is upstream, not in a cloud.
starting_goal: Restore the stream's morning sound
friction_source: A ritual anchored to a sound; the sound's cause is physical and findable
character_want: Pip: competent-wanted — his day runs on rituals he can't defend but deeply needs
power_usage: Nimbus's drizzle-as-instrument (patterned drops on leaves) approximates but never matches the burble; expressive, not a fix
escalation: Escalation by kind: drizzle rhythms -> drumming on bark -> Pip following the stream upstream while the burble degrades further, a sound-map in reverse
emotional_beat: The branch lifts; the burble returns; but Nimbus's drizzle-song was close enough that Pip asks for it sometimes — the imitation becomes its own ritual
rewatch_detail: The burble's pitch drops scene by scene; the repair restores it mid-note, audibly
distinctness_note: Sound as the stakes; the power fails as a fix but succeeds as a gift

title: Washing Day Shadows
logline: The laundry line snaps on washing day. Drying must wait a full day — unless the waiting becomes the game: the hanging sheets are the best shadow-theater screens in the world.
starting_goal: Get the washing dry despite the broken line
friction_source: A routine chore blocked for a whole day; patience required, play available
character_want: Nimbus: wanted — waiting is his weakness; turning waiting into play is his survival strategy
power_usage: None — drying with wind is possible but refused: wet sheets plus sun plus time do the job (patience premise, not power premise)
escalation: Escalation by kind: improvised lines -> sheets as tents -> the shadow show that draws the snail audience and delays folding entirely
emotional_beat: The washing dries during the show's finale; folding happens by lantern light, willingly — the chore was lost, the day was not
rewatch_detail: The shadow show retells the pair's own first meeting in silhouette — continuity for rewatchers only
distinctness_note: Chore-blocked becomes stage-found; refusal of the obvious power solution is written into the premise

title: Nothing Happened Today
logline: Pip's map ritual requires recording one change per day. Today: nothing changed. Nimbus can't bear the empty page and moves one pebble, perfectly. Pip spots the forgery immediately.
starting_goal: Nimbus wants Pip's map-ritual to have its daily entry
friction_source: A kindness that requires forgery; a ritual that requires truth
character_want: Pip: wanted — the ritual is his way of loving the place; Nimbus: needed — an empty page feels like a day he failed to be in
power_usage: None
escalation: Escalation by kind: one moved pebble -> a second, more convincing change -> an entire staged 'landslide' of three pebbles that fools no one
emotional_beat: Pip writes the true entry: 'Nimbus moved a pebble for me.' It becomes the most-quoted line of the map
rewatch_detail: The pebble's original and new positions match the friendship-edge pattern from the border episode
distinctness_note: The smallest possible stakes (one pebble) carrying a full honesty story; nothing breaks, nothing gets wet

title: The Noon Crossing That Stopped
logline: The snail crosses the path at noon, always. Today it stopped at the edge and will not move. Worry, observation, then discovery: eggs. The path must learn to bend.
starting_goal: Find out why the snail broke its crossing ritual
friction_source: A beloved routine stops for an invisible, living reason
character_want: Both: needed — the snail's trust is a duty; misreading its signals would betray it
power_usage: None; mist for the eggs is considered and refused — the nest must not be disturbed
escalation: Escalation by kind: tempting lettuce trail (ignored) -> escort plan (refused by the snail's stillness) -> quiet observation that finally sees the eggs
emotional_beat: The path is re-marked to curve around the nest; the noon crossing becomes the noon guard, and the village notes approve the new map
rewatch_detail: The eggs are visible (tiny pearls) in the nest from the second scene — shown, not announced
distinctness_note: The world's routine outranks the characters'; care means changing infrastructure, not the animal

title: The Shade That Moved
logline: The old tree's leaves grew denser; Nimbus's nap-shade spot migrated three body-lengths east. He keeps drifting back to where the shade was. Habit versus canopy, all afternoon.
starting_goal: Nimbus wants his nap spot back
friction_source: A slow environmental change outran a fast habit
character_want: Nimbus: wanted — the spot was HIS; the tree didn't ask
power_usage: None
escalation: Escalation by kind: drifting back -> marking the old spot with pebbles (the shade ignores the pebbles) -> napping in protest in full sun and waking up cranky and slightly steamed-off
emotional_beat: The new shade at dusk is longer and cooler and fits two; the old spot is retired with a small ceremony and a pebble crown
rewatch_detail: The tree's shadow rotates measurably across the episode — a sundial the episode is staged on
distinctness_note: Growth of the world as gentle antagonist; the cloud is beaten by a tree's patience
